subject: CrescentCare on-prem: KV cache growth causing pipeline noise — exec briefing requested
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma.carter@crescentcare.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Ops <it_ops@crescentcare.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: We’re seeing p95 spikes + 502 bursts on our on‑prem cluster (urgent)

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Apologize for the early note — over the last 36 hours our VPC/on‑prem deployment of Redwood has started showing intermittent p95 latency spikes and a cluster of 502s during peak ingest windows (03:00–06:00 UTC). We see token decode stalls and a correlated rise in KV cache resident size on the primary nodes. This is impacting a small but critical set of inference pipelines (clinical triage).

What we’ve observed: 
- p95 latency up from ~180ms to ~1.2s during nightly batch window
- 502 error bursts (20–40 per hour) primarily from worker set A
- KV cache resident memory grows steadily overnight; manual restart of serving runtime reduces errors for ~6–8 hours then it resurfaces

We need Redwood on this ASAP — we're evaluating customer impact and I’ll need an exec‑level status for our CTO tomorrow morning. Can you confirm next steps and whether this looks like cache growth/leak or a workload pattern mismatch? Attached are aggregated KV stats and one stack trace from the 03:12 UTC failure.

Attachments: [Attachment: crescent_kv_stats.csv (text/csv, 48KB)], [Attachment: nightly-stacktrace.txt (text/plain, 12KB)]

— Emma
Emma Carter
Director of Platform Engineering, CrescentCare
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Carter <emma.carter@crescentcare.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: We’re seeing p95 spikes + 502 bursts on our on‑prem cluster (urgent)

Thanks for the details, Emma — and for the attachments. I’m escalating this to our SRE and CS leads now.

Immediate plan: 
1) Marissa will triage logs and confirm whether the KV growth is due to prefix miss amplification or a leak in our cache eviction path.
2) We’ll coordinate a controlled restart window if needed (targeting a low‑impact time you confirm).
3) If we identify a regression or kernel/quantization interaction, we’ll prepare a hotfix and an exec summary for your CTO.

Laura / Marissa / Naomi — please jump in with early findings. Emma — can you confirm the low‑impact maintenance window between 22:00–23:30 UTC tonight if we need to restart the serving runtime?

Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Emma Carter <emma.carter@crescentcare.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: We’re seeing p95 spikes + 502 bursts on our on‑prem cluster (urgent)

Quick triage update (initial):
- I pulled the node metrics and KV eviction traces from the period Emma highlighted. The KV cache resident set increases roughly linearly during the nightly window, but eviction churn is low — appears like active entries are accumulating.
- Stacktrace points at decoder worker OOM path followed by abrupt process restart; looking like a cascading effect when KV lookups exceed memory/fragmentation threshold.
- No immediate evidence of a new model rollout or config change from CrescentCare side in the timeseries we've got; request logs show higher concurrent long‑context requests between 03:00–04:00 UTC (likely prepipelines).

Proposed mitigations (short window):
- Enable aggressive eviction policy (reduce max_resident to current mean + 20%) and restart serving runtime on the affected shard. This should bring p95 back within SLA for the short term.
- Add a temporary workload throttle for very long contexts (cut context >12k tokens) for the nightly pipeline to reduce amplification.
- After stabilizing, we’ll run a small reproduction with a mirrored workload to confirm whether root cause is cache pressure vs. pathological prefix growth.

Attachments: [Attachment: marissa_kv_trace_snippet.txt (text/plain, 9KB)]

I can start the restart tonight if Emma approves the window; otherwise we can wait until your confirmed maintenance slot.

— Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Emma Carter <emma.carter@crescentcare.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: We’re seeing p95 spikes + 502 bursts on our on‑prem cluster (urgent)

Thanks team — this is getting flagged to leadership and I’ll prepare a short exec brief for CrescentCare’s CTO call tomorrow (11 Sep, 10:00 UTC). 

Action items I’m taking: 
- Draft 1‑page summary with timeline, immediate mitigations, risk level, and expected customer impact (to be sent to Emma and their CTO).
- Schedule an exec‑level 25 minute sync for tomorrow — Karthik, please confirm you’ll be on the call to cover contract/credits if there’s a material SLA breach.
- Marissa: proceed with the short window restart tonight at 22:30 UTC if Emma confirms. Naomi: please prepare a customer note template and a proposed temporary SLA credit if we exceed the agreed p95 breach threshold.

Emma — appreciate confirmation of the 22:30–23:00 UTC window for the restart. If CrescentCare prefers a later time, we’ll accommodate but want to avoid more degradation overnight.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Carter <emma.carter@crescentcare.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood_field@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: We’re seeing p95 spikes + 502 bursts on our on‑prem cluster (urgent)

Emma — quick final note after the exec sync today: we performed the controlled restart on 11 Sep at 22:34 UTC with the temporary eviction policy in place; p95 dropped back to baseline and 502s subsided. Marissa’s team will run the mirrored workload test this week and we’ll share results no later than EOD Friday.

Next steps for Redwood / CrescentCare partnership: 
- Short term: keep temporary eviction & throttle in place until we complete reproduction + root cause.
- Medium term: we propose a targeted config change and a lightweight patch to improve eviction heuristics for long‑context workloads. We attached a proposed runbook for the suggested changes and an initial impact estimate.

Attachments: [Attachment: proposed-runbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 98KB)]
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CrescentCare-Incidents/notes-cc-kv-cache

If you want, we can escalate this to a joint postmortem once the reproduction is complete; otherwise we’ll treat as a high‑priority tuning ticket with regular status updates.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the follow‑up and loop in our integrations partner if we need hardware‑level diagnostics.

Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
